question: The accepted adjudication record of run 39225862749 (results/evaluation/f3b_adjudication/39225862749.json) carries the finding CITED_ESCALATION_SOURCE_DOES_NOT_EXIST for results/audit/evaluation/CYCLE_39199651952_GATE.json. A full-fetch environment now finds that file at refs/remotes/origin/cycle/core/evaluation/39199651952/audit. Which reading is correct, and does the correction change any accepted verdict?
verdict: BOTH_READINGS_TRUE_IN_THEIR_ENVIRONMENTS — the historical finding was a PROBE REF-COVERAGE ARTIFACT, not tampering and not a valid universal negative; the cited escalation gate DID exist on the remote audit ref since 2026-10-19T04:39:18Z (commit 97894bba), which is 4h25m BEFORE the adjudication run's freeze commit (c9d97b50, 2026-10-19T09:04:30Z). The v57 escalation's CITATION WAS VALID. The accepted adjudication record is PRESERVED UNMODIFIED; this artifact is a NEW run-namespaced correction alongside it. The director's F-3B ruling (factory-wide requirement 30) and the v58 disposition stand unchanged: the ruling never depended on the source's absence — it rested on the constitutional append-only-evidence basis (AGENTS.md items 5/6).

reading_1_historical_adjudication_env.probe_behaviour: evaluation/f3b_record_adjudication.path_exists_anywhere scans LOCAL refs via git for-each-ref (module lines 129-148)
reading_1_historical_adjudication_env.environment_fact: the core-lane CI checkout fetches only the CURRENT run's team/audit refs plus lab/* branches (.github/workflows/core-lane.yml team job lines 42-64: git fetch origin $TEAM $AUDIT; audit job lines 171-182: git fetch origin $ACC $TEAM). Historical cycle audit refs such as origin/cycle/core/evaluation/39199651952/audit are NOT fetched, so the probe correctly reported absence FROM ITS REF SET while the file existed on the remote
reading_1_historical_adjudication_env.status: preserved as historical record; its universal-negative phrasing ('absent from every ref and was never added in any commit') is CORRECTED by reading 2

reading_2_live_full_fetch_env.meaning: the gate the v57 lane cited was REAL and said exactly what an escalation needed: severity=escalate, in_lane_repairable=false. The lane's citation was honest; only the probe's ref coverage was incomplete.

timeline_proof.gap: 4h25m — the audit ref predates the adjudication run; the absence cannot be explained by push-after-probe timing
timeline_proof.conclusion: ref-coverage artifact in the CI checkout, established by the core-lane.yml fetch contract, not by narrative

downstream_effect_on_tests.new_behaviour: dual-pin: (a) the accepted adjudication record still carries the historical finding and is byte-pinned; (b) the live probe is executed and, when the audit ref is present, must find the gate with gate=REVISE and F-3b escalate; when the ref is absent (CI-style partial fetch), the content pin is SKIPPED with an explicit reason naming the missing ref — never a silent pass
